text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch industry sees investments growing strongly next year. (p1)
- Electrical engineering conglomerate Detron takes over glass fibre cabling group Meijsen Groep. (p1)
- Colllapse of sports-only television channel Sport7 will cost Endemol management Joop van den Ende and John de Mol no more than 80 million guilders. (p1)
- Transport group Pakhoed sells its storage terminal in Neuss, Germany to Retroplus International. (p3)
- Insurance sector watchdog and insurers' association agree to create safety net for life insurers in financial difficulties. (p3)
- Paper and office products group KNP BT's paper making unit KNP Leykam gets a 480 million guilder loan from European Investment Bank EIB. (p4)
- State-owned broadcasting relay company Nozema, to be privatised in 1998, will sell off its 22 pct stake in cable company Casema. (p4)
- Brokerage Van der Moolen is to take over private loan broker Jonker & Co. (p11)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Russia and the Netherlands to open talks soon on returning famous Koenigs art collection to the Netherlands. (p1)
- Economic affairs minister Hans Wijers maintains his objections to football association's monopoly on football broadcasting rights. (p1)
- U.S. software house Datastream takes over Rotterdam-based SQL-Systems. (p2)
- Dutch carrier KLM to pay some 800 million guilders in buy-back of 17.2 million state-owned KLM shares. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Fresh Dutch-French diplomatic tension looms after French police fail to intervene when French truckers molest Dutch hauliers. (p1)
- Queen Beatrix and guests forced to evacuate Amsterdam's New Church at gala exhibition opening after bomb hoax. (p1)
- The Dutch drop from sixth to ninth place in world rankings of deregulated economies. (p3)
- Dutch PTT (KPN) fully owns express transporter GD Express Worldwide. (p23)
TROUW
- Utility company EDON to rival PTT Telecom by setting up its own call centre. (p7)
- Royal Dutch/Shell needs more time to reflect on options on dismantling oil rig Brent Spar. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Parliamentary Labour party clashes with Transport Minister Annemarie Jorritsma over route of proposed high-speed rail link. (p1)
- Shell calls off grocery retail cooperation with Ahold supermarket chain Albert Heijn due to difference of opinion about costs. (p13)
